head_commit.message:
feat(37): OCR goes through ML Kit, because the .so has no OCR engine at all

a2 has never reached an OCR engine. Two separate facts, both measured:

1. THE NATIVE PATH CANNOT WORK IN THIS BUILD. gs_mobile_ocr is a stub:

       set_err("no OCR engine is compiled into this mobile build; run OCR
               through the provider path or use a gs-ocr-enabled build");

   The Tesseract archives that would fix it are cross-compiled and verified
   (item 2: 12,282,294 bytes stripped) but are NOT linked into gs-ffi, and the
   on-demand module meant to carry them is BLOCKED.

2. THE PATH THAT SHIPS ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS NEVER CALLED.
   `libs.mlkit.text.recognition` 16.0.1 is a bundled dependency in the app
   module, and nothing in android/app/src/main/java referenced it. ML Kit was the
   decided primary OCR path and had no call site at all.

So MlKitOcr is added and a2 exercises it, and the test no longer claims to test
something that does not exist.

a2 NOW ASSERTS BOTH HALVES

  - the native path REFUSES, with a legible reason. Previously a null from
    gs_mobile_ocr would have been indistinguishable from OCR succeeding on an
    image it never opened.
  - ML Kit reads the generated fixture and the output contains "INV-4471"

An image with no text returns "" from MlKitOcr, deliberately different from a
failure, so "no text here" and "OCR did not run" cannot look the same. A missing
or empty file throws.

Synchronous by design: the callers are Kotlin, and the JUnit tests are not
coroutines. The work runs on ML Kit's own executor and Tasks.await blocks the
caller, so a main-thread caller must not use it -- stated in the KDoc rather than
left to be discovered.

This is the honest reading of the state, and it is also the faster one: linking
Tesseract into the .so is a build.rs change with its own prebuilt-wiring, and ML
Kit is already in the APK.

head_commit.message:
fix(36): GsNativeException did not exist — every native failure was a silent null

Run 36576882672, the first device run that got as far as CALLING OCR (the
fixture now lands, so a2 stopped skipping and started failing):

    java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Didn't find class
      "com.grapsee.gsai.native.GsNativeException" on path: DexPathList[...]

The JNI bridge has thrown that class by name since it was written:

    env.find_class("com/grapsee/gsai/native/GsNativeException")

and the class was never created. The note beside the call was wrong:

    "If the class is missing, the entry points still return their explicit
     failure value, so Kotlin never sees a success-shaped null."

A Java entry point returning String returns NULL on failure. A null is not an
explicit failure value to Kotlin code declared `: String` -- it is a null that
arrives in code expecting a string. So every native failure in the history of
this bridge has been a null reaching a caller, and the reason the native side
formats as "GsNative.<what>: <reason>" has been discarded every time.

Two things fixed:
  - GsNativeException.kt, with operation and reason kept as fields so a caller
    can log or branch on the engine's own words rather than on a message string
  - the wrong comment in jni.rs, so the next reader is not told the class is
    legitimately optional. The find_class guard STAYS, so a host that genuinely
    lacks the class degrades to the null return instead of aborting.

ALSO CONFIRMED IN THIS RUN

    asked  -> What is the capital of France? Answer with one word.
    replied -> Paris.

The <|im_end|> strip works. Run 36566952196 had "Paris. <|im_end|>".
